title: Squeezing More from Limited Data with Recursive Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2608.26973v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Pre-training under limited data requires a different view of scaling than web-scale language modeling. With a fixed data budget but relatively abundant compute, increasing parameter count helps only up to an optimal scale; beyond that point, models overfit and generalization worsens. We study this behavior across 10M-100M word pre-training budgets, two corpora, and multiple downstream evaluations, and find that optimal size depends strongly on both the data budget and the downstream target. We argue that standard Transformers scale down poorly to this setting, because embeddings consume a large fraction of the parameter budget and per-token computation is tied to representational capacity. To address this coupling, we study recursive Transformers, reusing a shared block across depth to scale compute, together with factorized embeddings to reduce vocabulary-map parameters. translated_title: 在有限数据下利用递归Transformer挖掘更多潜力
translated_abstract: 在有限数据下进行预训练，需要与网络规模语言建模不同的扩展视角。在固定数据预算但相对充足的计算资源下，增加参数数量仅有助于达到最优规模；超过该点后，模型会过拟合，泛化能力变差。我们研究了1000万至1亿词预训练预算、两个语料库和多种下游评估中的这一行为，发现最优规模强烈依赖于数据预算和下游目标。我们认为标准Transformer在此设置下扩展效果不佳，因为嵌入层消耗了大量参数预算，且每个token的计算与表示能力紧密耦合。为解决这一耦合问题，我们研究了递归Transformer，通过深度复用共享块来扩展计算，并结合分解嵌入以减少词汇映射参数。我们训练了三个递归模型，发现它们优于标准模型。
tldr: 该论文提出递归Transformer和分解嵌入，在有限数据预算下通过复用共享块扩展计算并减少嵌入参数，显著提升模型泛化性能。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes recursive Transformers with factorized embeddings to scale compute via shared block reuse and reduce embedding parameters, improving generalization under limited data budgets.
